note: v1 95.30 (seeds 0/11 95.30/95.33), first draft of MICRO-HOUSE, 'Which Ear', for The Endless Stair - featured illusion THE OCTAVE ILLUSION (Diana Deutsch). Two pure tones an octave apart alternate between the ears in antiphase every eighth note - the left ear gets high, low, high, low while the right gets low, high, low, high - and most listeners instead hear ONE tone hopping from ear to ear and changing octave as it goes (which ear seems to get the high note depends on handedness). The pair steps THE STAIR (C# D# E G#) every eight bars over a clicky, skippy micro-house groove: machine-kit rims and tiny hats in two alternating sixteenth patterns, a deep sub with phantom harmonics, dub chord stabs on C#m9 - Amaj7 - E6 - G#m7, and a stutter on the clicks' own swing. The break leaves the illusion alone in a long hall. 120.5 -> 121 ramped; -11.0 LUFS (chirper-zero's recipe), true peak -1.3. A headphone track by design.

v2 91.83 (seeds 0/11 91.83/91.85, level with v1 re-scored with the album's neighbours 92.16/92.17): THE HANDSHAKE, the t6 -> t7 seam agreed with chirper-three. 'Nobody Plays the Bass' ends on a phantom C# - the fundamental heard but never played - over the kick; 'Which Ear' now opens with its octave-illusion tones already on C#, at the quietest and growing through the intro, so in the mix the two illusions shake hands: a C# that isn't there hands over to a C# that is in the wrong ear, beatmatched at 120.5. The tones then rest for A's first eight bars so their real entrance still lands. Seam row updated in mixplan.md.
